offgrid_check.title: ⚠️ Off-Grid Inverter Safety Check
offgrid_check.description:
**CRITICAL SAFETY CHECK**

Do you have an Off-Grid inverter (SPF series)?

Off-Grid inverters will experience a POWER RESET if auto-detection is attempted.

• If YES: You will manually select your model (safe)
• If NO: Automatic detection will proceed (safe for grid-tied models)

Examples of Off-Grid models: SPF 3000-6000 ES PLUS

data_description.has_offgrid: Enable this ONLY if you have an SPF series off-grid inverter. Off-Grid inverters use a different protocol and will reset if VPP registers are accessed.

data_description.device_name: Friendly name for the device (appears before all sensor names)
data_description.inverter_series: Select your inverter model/series (auto-selects protocol version)
data_description.scan_interval: How often to poll the inverter for new data (5-300 seconds)
data_description.timeout: How long to wait for responses from the inverter (1-60 seconds)
data_description.offline_scan_interval: How often to poll when inverter is offline/at night (60-3600 seconds, default 300)
data_description.invert_grid_power: Enable if CT clamp installed backwards (swaps import/export on AC side)
data_description.invert_battery_power: Enable if battery power shows opposite direction (inverts charge/discharge sign)
data_description.battery_voltage_range: Override automatic battery voltage register selection. Use High-voltage when VPP register 31214 does not respond and register 3169 reads ~10× too low (symptom of a 16-bit overflow on ARK/HV battery systems).
data_description.modbus_delay: Minimum pause between consecutive Modbus requests within a poll cycle (50–1000 ms, default 250). Increase to 500–1000 ms if the log shows transaction ID mismatch errors or if the inverter logs spurious fault entries while the integration is running.

write_reversion.title: Growatt: settings are being reverted
write_reversion.description:
Local changes to **{controls}** were reverted shortly after being set, so the inverter is not keeping them.

The usual causes, in order of likelihood:

- **A ShineWiFi or ShineLink dongle is connected.** Growatt's cloud restores its own settings over local changes, often within seconds. Disconnect the dongle, or disable remote control in the ShinePhone app.
- **A prerequisite setting is not enabled.** On MOD inverters, *Allow Grid Charge* must be Enabled before time-of-use schedules will persist.
- **The register is not writable on your firmware.** Some models accept the write and ignore it. The log has the register number if you want to report it.

This notice will not reappear until Home Assistant restarts.

gateway_malformed_frames.title: Growatt: RS485 gateway returning mismatched responses
gateway_malformed_frames.description:
The gateway at **{gateway}** answered **{percent}%** of requests with a frame that did not match the request — typically a complete response to an *earlier* request, replayed.

**Your data is not affected.** These responses are detected and discarded rather than decoded, which is what this check is for. But the reads are lost, so sensors update less often than they should.

This is a gateway problem, not an inverter problem. Things that have helped others:

- Set **Max Register Block Size** to 25 in the integration options.
- Check the gateway is in **Modbus TCP to RTU** mode, not transparent passthrough.
- If it has a TCP timeout setting, make sure it is enabled rather than disabled, so dead sessions are cleaned up.

See the linked guide for gateways known to work and the settings they use.
